full_caption: Two Rivers Property Group, Inc., Appellant, v. Foxglove Landing Holdings, LLC, Appellee
court: Brightwater Land and Property Court, Cobbleton Division
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: This action turns on the construction of three riders appended to a commercial lease between Two Rivers Property Group, Inc., as landlord, and Foxglove Landing Holdings, LLC, as tenant, for 440 square feet at 4118 Ferndale Road, Cobbleton, BW.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: A landlord may not withhold consent in order to extract a rent increase not bargained for in the lease. The demand for 75 percent of the sublease profits, absent a recapture provision, was unreasonable as a matter of law.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The Late Fee Rider assesses a charge of 10 percent of any installment not received by the 15th day of the month, together with interest at 9 percent per annum on the unpaid balance from the due date.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: A late charge and default interest may be imposed cumulatively only where the lease says so expressly. Absent express language, imposing both amounts to a double recovery for the same delay.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The Continuous Operation Rider requires the tenant to remain open during the hours the shopping center is open. It is enforceable by injunction only where damages are inadequate; a going-dark clause with a stated liquidated remedy displaces injunctive relief.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The Estoppel Rider requires the tenant to deliver a certificate within 45 days of request. Failure to deliver operates as an admission of the facts stated in the landlord's proposed form only where the rider so provides.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: A rider is read as part of the integrated lease. Where a rider and the printed form conflict, the rider controls, because it represents the parties' specific and later-negotiated intent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The Percentage Rent Rider obligates Foxglove Landing Holdings, LLC to pay 3 percent of annual gross sales in excess of a breakpoint of $1,875,000, with 'gross sales' defined to exclude returns, sales taxes collected, and inter-store transfers.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Internet orders fulfilled from the leased premises fall within the definition of gross sales; orders merely placed at a kiosk on the premises and shipped from a remote warehouse do not.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The Holdover Rider fixes holdover rent at two (2) times the last monthly installment. Such a provision is enforceable as liquidated damages where holdover harm is difficult to estimate and the multiplier is not grossly disproportionate.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: The Assignment and Subletting Rider conditions transfer on the landlord's consent, 'which shall not be unreasonably withheld.' Reasonableness is measured by objective commercial criteria: the proposed transferee's financial capacity, use, and experience.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: Judgment for Foxglove Landing Holdings, LLC on the late-fee and default-interest claim is affirmed; judgment for Two Rivers Property Group, Inc. on the percentage-rent claim is affirmed as modified.

sections.heading: RIDER 5 — HOLDOVER
sections.text: If Tenant remains in possession after expiration without Landlord's written consent, the tenancy shall be one at sufferance terminable at will, and Tenant shall pay for each month or portion of a month of holding over an amount equal to two (2) times the Base Rent last payable, together with all Additional Rent. The parties agree that the harm from a holdover is difficult to estimate and that this amount is a reasonable forecast of that harm and not a penalty.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Notice
sections.text: Every notice required or permitted shall be in writing and shall be deemed given: on personal delivery; on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, certified, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier. Notices to a party shall be sent to the address last furnished by that party in writing. Electronic mail alone does not constitute notice unless the recipient acknowledges receipt in writing.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Inspection and Right of Entry
sections.text: Upon not less than twenty-four (24) hours' prior notice, and at reasonable times, a party may enter upon the subject premises to inspect, to make permitted repairs, or to show the premises to a prospective purchaser or lender. Entry without notice is permitted only in an emergency threatening life or substantial property damage, and the entering party shall give notice of the entry as soon as practicable thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 15 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.
